hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation (gate self-test on this piece's surface)
hard_gates.evidence: The product itself showed no real leak. I probed as Al Noor against Gulf Steel with 65 requests (isolation-probe.txt) and found 0 of 26 B markers. The requests covered user records and their sub-resources (access, default-company, sign-ins, passkeys), companies and branches, the company logo file path, the company-profile report in Arabic, the workplace switch to B's company, B's roles and role copy, and B's saved view (own and shared). They also covered PUT /me/preferences in all four language/digit combinations with B's ids in the body and tenant headers, tenant query parameters, and CSV, XLSX and PDF prints in Arabic. A non-marker check also passed: A's preference answers, headers included, did not change after B switched five times. Copy-role answers 404 for B's id and for a random id. All 17 tenant tables have RLS enabled and forced. erp_app is not superuser and has no BYPASSRLS. With no tenant context it sees 0 users. The fix for the r8 gap holds: plant L5 (a process-wide count kept in a temp file and sent in a response header) was caught by G1NonInterference, with 8 findings in both directions, English and Arabic (plants-B2b-L5-gates.log). MISSED: plants L4 and L6 on PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, the shell's own endpoint (plant-server-B1-L4-L6.diff). L4 sends the count of every tenant's Arabic switches back as a cookie value. L6 sends the time of anyone's previous switch in a header. All 169 gate tests passed with them in place, including G1NonInterference (9 m 57 s), G1HttpIsolation (31 m 8 s) and G1ProcessState (plants-B1-gates.log). On the planted build tenant A's cookie went from 2 to 8 while tenant B switched five times. A's header also gave the exact time of B's last switch (plant-B1-live-demo.txt).

biggest_gap.title: The G1 non-interference check still misses a cross-tenant leak that carries no marker when it travels in a cookie value or as a time in a response header: it blanks every Set-Cookie value and every time before comparing
biggest_gap.detail: Round 9 closed round 8's gap: response headers are now compared, configuration is sealed, and a changing count in a header is caught by the change probe (my L5 was caught). But NonInterference.NormalizeHeaders still replaces the value of every Set-Cookie with <value> and every time in any header with <time>. The change probe compares the same normalised answers, so it sees no change either. A process-wide count sent in a cookie, or the time of another tenant's last action sent in a header, is invisible to all three G1 checks. The marker attack looks only for B's ids and names, and ProcessState does not see state kept outside the process (a temp file, a shared cache). I planted both kinds on PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, the shell's own Arabic-switch endpoint. All 169 gate tests passed, and on the running build tenant A watched tenant B's activity: A's count went from 2 to 8, and A saw the exact time of B's last switch. Real code produces exactly this: rate-limit or 'last activity' cookies, Last-Modified or ETag-style timestamps of shared caches, and 'recently changed' stamps. Every later module (invoices, stock, journals) inherits the blind spot. The machinery is shared with p00, but the fault sits on p04's surface, as in r8. Fix: (1) In NormalizeHeaders, blank only the values of the product's own reviewed credential cookies (the session and trusted-device cookies, from a reviewed list). Compare every other cookie value, and feed changing values to the change probe. (2) Replace times only in Date and the declared print stamp. Leave every other time in a header as sent, and judge it by how it changes (alone against with the other tenant in between, with a pause between calls). Apply the same to times in bodies. (3) Add both plants to the non-interference self-tests, with a ratchet count of cookie values compared.
biggest_gap.evidence: In a clone at a2c3400, apply gauntlet/evidence/p04-shell/r9/plants/plant-server-B1-L4-L6.diff. Run the gate tests with filter 'Load!=Timing&Process!=self-http&Process!=self-company&Process!=self-noninterference' (plants/run-plant.sh B1): 169 of 169 pass, including G1NonInterferenceTests (9 m 57 s), G1HttpIsolationTests (31 m 8 s) and G1ProcessStateTests (plants/plants-B1-gates.log). Live: on the planted build (./erp up), drivers/plant-B1-live.mjs shows admin@alnoor.example's erp.tip cookie at 1 and 2. admin@gulfsteel.example then switches five times (3 to 7), and Al Noor's next switch gets erp.tip=8 with X-Arabic-Previous-Switch equal to Gulf Steel's last switch time (plants/plant-B1-live-demo.txt). For contrast, the same count in a plain header (plant-server-B2b-L5-only.diff) is caught with 8 findings (plants/plants-B2b-L5-gates.log). The normaliser is in tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G1/NonInterference.cs: NormalizeHeaders, CookieValueRegex, and TimeRegex/HttpDateRegex applied to every header.
